title: Resolve Helm lockfile contention causing on-prem upgrade failures and implement safe fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported failed on-prem upgrades where the operator's Helm orchestration path deadlocks on a per-release lockfile. Symptoms: upgrade job remains stuck in 'in progress' for >30 minutes, nodeagent re-applies partial config, and KV-cache entries diverge leading to request 500s for a subset of tenants. This ticket is to implement a mitigation, hotfix release, and a post-upgrade reconciliation runbook.
impact_summary: Affects Private/VPC customers performing rolling upgrades. Approx 6 customers escalated in last 72 hours (two P1 enterprise accounts). Observed user-facing errors: 500s and degraded routing for model inference, some customers reporting inability to complete upgrades and requiring manual rollback of Helm release. Severity: customer-visible outage and potential data drift in operator CR status fields.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy operator-2.14.0 to test cluster with multi-namespace private deployments
2) Trigger Helm rolling upgrade of operator chart with concurrent nodeagent changes (simulate autoscaler modifications)
3) Observe helm upgrade start; one replica obtains a helm lock and the upgrade stalls when two controller reconciliation loops attempt to claim the same release lock
4) After ~10-30m, some CRs show partial status updates and KV cache snapshots diverge between replicas resulting in API 500s for in-flight requests
investigation_notes: - Root cause: race on release-level lockfile implemented in the operator. The lock acquire path doesn't honor context cancellation in one code path, causing goroutine leak and lock hold until timeout. Under load, this leads to multiple controllers waiting and partially applying manifests.

- Secondary impact: partial writes to custom resources and kvcache result in inconsistent leader-follower state; the automatic drift-detection wasn't aggressive enough to detect and reconcile short-lived partial upgrades.
- Repro in staging with high reconciliation frequency at 250ms intervals; failure correlates with concurrent CR updates and a long-running pre-upgrade hook in a customer chart.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation: publish an emergency runbook for customers to 1) set operator.reconciliation.pause=true before attempting upgrades, 2) increase helm release timeout to 30m, and 3) if stuck, run 'kubectl delete job <helm-job>' + restart operator pod to force lock release. We will also provide a support script to detect stuck locks and safely force-unlock with a leader check.
fix_summary: Code fix: make lock acquire path context-aware and add a bounded retry with exponential backoff. Add atomic compare-and-swap metadata on the Helm lock CR to prevent stale holders being considered active. Add post-upgrade reconciliation worker that scans recently-upgraded releases and triggers CR-level rehydration (idempotent) to ensure KV cache and CR status converge.
qa_plan: Unit tests for lock path and simulated concurrent acquisition. Integration tests in staging using a multi-replica operator with synthetic pre-upgrade hooks. End-to-end smoke test: perform rolling upgrade across 3 namespaces with traffic generator; assert no 500s and final CR status matches expected desired state.
rollout_plan: 1) Cut operator-2.14.1-hotfix branch with lock-path fix and reconciliation worker. 2) Deploy to internal canary (single customer-like cluster) and monitor for 24h. 3) Release to COS (customer-facing) channels as patch; recommend customers schedule upgrades after installing patch or apply our live unlock script. 4) For customers on managed Dedicated/Hosted, perform automatic patching with opt-out toggle. Hotfix window recommended: 2025-02-20 18:00-22:00 UTC.
post_release_runbook: - Detect stuck helm locks: kubectl get helmlocks -A | grep stuck; run support script with --dry-run first. - If forced unlock required: scale down operator replicas to 0, delete lock CRs, scale up operator, run reconciliation job. - Verify kvcache snapshots match leader via 'redwood-ctl kvcache-diff'. - Communicate to customer with steps and timing, and mark ticket as resolved after 48h of stability.
communications: Customer comms draft posted to #cust-escalations: short summary, mitigation steps, ETA for hotfix and recommendation to pause upgrades until patch is applied.
Support playbook: Slack template, runbook checklist, and one-click support script (Gist link) prepared for SEs.
Postmortem note to be drafted after stabilization: include timeline, root cause, and compensating controls.
